features.title: Verified principal directory and issuer identity
features.description: Resolve people by verified issuer and exact subject, with explicit directory registration and historical references.
user_capabilities: Inspect a scoped user roster
Register known identities for access review
Keep identical subjects from different issuers separate
features.core_note: Protocol claims take precedence over presentation-filtered OIDC user data. The auth probe exposes principalIssuer; invalid present protocol evidence does not fall back to a guessed issuer. Registration does not simulate a verified sign-in.
features.rust_note: OIDC links use issuer+subject and durable principal IDs. At this source snapshot kernel.rs has removed its synthetic-token shortcut and auth_user refuses anonymous introspection, but the compatibility response still substitutes internal principal ID into user.sub and omits verified issuer; deployed remediation was not rechecked.

features.title: External OIDC browser sign-in
features.description: Authenticate browser sessions through configured identity providers.
user_capabilities: Sign in through an external identity provider
Sign out of the browser session
Use configured provider discovery and callback routing
features.core_note: OIDC middleware, provider configuration and verified claims feed the common request identity; mock mode is a separate explicit deployment predicate.
features.rust_note: Actual signin/callback/signout routes use discovery, PKCE/state and registered issuer JWT verification with stored sessions. Wiring is source evidence, not a live provider-login receipt.

features.title: Invited local user accounts
features.description: Provide controlled password login when an external identity provider is unavailable or alongside a hybrid deployment.
user_capabilities: Invite an account by email
Accept an expiring single-use invitation
Sign in with a local password
features.core_note: The local store uses scrypt password hashes and hashed one-time invitation/reset tokens. LOCAL_AUTH plus MOCK_OIDC or missing signing configuration fails at setup rather than opening access.
features.rust_note: LocalAuth implements durable accounts, password derivation, account-enumeration-resistant verification and failure windows; people invitation/accept routes exist. The core local login page/API contract is not reproduced by those different HTTP surfaces.

features.title: Local session lifetime and revocation
features.description: Keep local sessions signed, bounded in lifetime and checked against current account state.
user_capabilities: Remain signed in within the rolling window
End the session by signing out
Lose session access when the account is disabled
features.core_note: Local cookies have a rolling 24-hour and absolute seven-day ceiling; session snapshots and versions prevent disabled accounts or superseded credentials retaining access.
features.rust_note: SessionStore persists digests, applies absolute/idle timeout, supports per-principal revocation, and is attached to local and OIDC sources. This is an equivalent lifecycle with a different cookie/store implementation.

features.title: Authenticator second factor and recovery codes
features.description: Require or opt into local TOTP authentication with one-use recovery codes.
user_capabilities: Enroll an authenticator
Confirm or disable the second factor
Use a recovery code
Let an administrator require or reset second-factor enrollment
features.core_note: TOTP secrets are encrypted; recovery codes are hashed and consumed. Setup/confirmation and administrative requirements are distinct routes.
features.rust_note: Bounded search across crates Rust/SQL source for totp, two-factor, 2fa and recovery-code found no implementation; inspected local accounts and session handlers contain password/session verification only.

features.title: Password reset and invitation delivery
features.description: Recover local account access without disclosing whether an email is registered.
user_capabilities: Request a password-reset link
Receive delivery when configured
Use a copyable administrator reinvitation link
features.core_note: Forgot-password response avoids account enumeration; active accounts receive expiring one-time reset material and administrator reinvitation invalidates earlier proof.
features.rust_note: Bounded crates Rust/SQL search for password-reset, recovery-code and forgot-password found no reset ceremony. LocalAuth password enrollment and generic invitations are narrower mechanisms, not this recovery flow.

features.title: Account status administration
features.description: Administer local account activation while keeping authorization changes consistent with account status.
user_capabilities: List local account metadata
Disable an account
Re-enable an account
Require a new invitation when appropriate
features.core_note: Administrative routes use current operator authority; disabling changes the session snapshot and prunes or invalidates related authority in the account transaction.
features.rust_note: People routes require root/kernel administration for suspend/reinstate/deactivate; directory state is read on entry and deactivation revokes sessions and other holders. Erase/export have self-or-admin checks.

features.title: Admin role and portal defaults
features.description: Give people who hold the admin role a separate set of screens for portal-wide defaults, while the same person keeps their ordinary screens for their own data.
user_capabilities: Hold the admin role on an ordinary account
Fall back to portal-default settings where a person has none of their own
features.core_note: ADR-174 Amendment A (2026-10-06) removed the separate configuration-only local account, its /login/admin sign-in and its route containment. Admin is the existing operator role (swarm_roles root/admin rows or the operator environment allowlist) on a person's own account. Amendment B (2026-10-06) built the Swarm Admin screens under /swarm-admin, each behind requiresOperator with the menu served as data by GET /api/admin/navigation: the home, AI defaults (ADR-173's fleet-default and capability panels), swarm logins (token-free vendor login status, GET /api/admin/swarm-logins), connectors (the ADR-067 marketplace catalog with enable/disable/remove/re-audit), budgets (every cap with POST /api/budgets/remove and budget.set/budget.remove audit events), shared knowledge (DELETE /api/rag/knowledge/:id over id-stamped chunks), devices (every remote client, bind/unbind, token rotation) and households (GET /api/admin/households, members managed where the operator is the household's admin). Still partial: the reserved portal-default owner (src/shared/portal-default, the owner-or-operator RLS helper) is adopted by no settings table yet beyond ADR-173's capability rows, so most per-person settings have no portal-wide default to fall back to.
features.rust_note: Not re-reviewed after ADR-174 Amendment A; the earlier mapping covered the removed configuration-only account.

features.title: Installer root election and transfer
features.description: Establish one recovery owner at installation and transfer that ownership through explicit authority.
user_capabilities: Complete a bound installer setup
Claim root on an empty installation
Transfer root without leaving the installation ownerless
features.core_note: Installer setup locks and validates an empty installation, origin and elected verified identity. Swarm roles refuse root removal and transfer atomically to the next owner.
features.rust_note: Kernel uses a fixed invariant root row, confirmed transfer and immutable root-removal refusal; daemon reconciles configured credentials to the durable owner. Core browser installer proof/origin flow differs.

features.title: Swarm roles and resource ownership gates

user_capabilities: Inspect own swarm role
Let an operator manage swarm roles
Use owned shared resources
features.core_note: Role store and operator/resource predicates are shared across route and dispatch callers. These platform gates do not confer catalog business permissions; legacy ownership tables can still be subject-only.
features.rust_note: Root flag plus deny/viewer/editor/admin package tiers and explicit capabilities provide related authority. The core swarm-role API and shared subject ownership semantics have different data/contracts.

features.title: Business tenants and explicit memberships

List own tenants
Add or remove a tenant member
Manage tenant membership roles
features.core_note: Tenant routes and connector-tenancy store require current membership/admin semantics for members and connection visibility. Business membership is explicit, not inherited merely from login-provider directory membership.
features.rust_note: Tenants library and HTTP member routes exist, but kernel admission currently confines a non-root caller to its principal.tenant rather than consulting active memberships for header selection. Root can choose arbitrary tenant scope; core membership-aware business authorization is not established by tenant storage alone.

Apply a revision-bound membership change
Inspect current membership catalog

Link a verified Entra login to an eligible existing local account
Use hybrid local and Microsoft login when configured

features.title: Application tiers, named roles and data permission scopes
features.description: Enforce application-owned permissions, scopes and fields within a coarse application access ceiling.
user_capabilities: Receive an explicit app role
Inspect effective permissions and denial reasons
Access only permitted operations and resource fields
features.core_note: Current registration binds catalog/source revisions; exact roles and permission denials resolve centrally. Runtime mounts and operation adapters enforce declared bot/tool/route policies. Package data adapters remain responsible for authoritative own/team/tenant and field enforcement; engine support is not proof every package declares a complete catalog.
features.rust_note: Rust has deny-precedence package tiers and whole-tuple capability scope/field coverage. These are narrower host capabilities, not an observed import/enforcement of core named role catalogs, team data scopes and package route policy bindings.

features.title: Scoped access administrators and auditors

Assign a read-only access auditor
Review access only inside the delegated scope

features.rust_note: Bounded crates source search for management scopes, management roles, @access-admin and @access-auditor found no corresponding templates. Existing root/kernel-admin people gates are broader and do not implement application+tenant access-management delegation.

features.title: Reviewed authorization changes and audit history
features.description: Require a current, bound preview before applying role, deny or directory assignment changes.
user_capabilities: Preview the exact access change
Apply a reviewed change atomically
Inspect scoped audit history
Retry an apply through an idempotent receipt
features.core_note: Management routes enforce same-origin writes, validated input, current actor/revision/source binding and expiring previews. Sensitive self/group changes require a verifier; sole-operator approval is a distinct durable path.
features.rust_note: Confirmed one-use grants and self-escalation refusal exist in Rust, with observer records. They do not reproduce core revision/source-bound access preview, apply receipt and scoped audit query semantics.

features.title: Experience composite roles and dependency grants
features.description: Assign exact experience role templates together with reviewed required and explicitly selected optional application roles.

Select optional dependencies explicitly
Review already-held access before applying
Upgrade or revoke an active composite assignment
Expand inactive assignment history
features.core_note: CompositeRoleEngine creates child previews through the existing authority and applies members plus provenance in one transaction. UI keeps optional choices unchecked, preserves unrelated existing grants, separates current assignments from collapsed revoked/expired history, and binds declaration/revision changes.
features.rust_note: Bounded crates Rust/SQL search for composite-role, composite assignment, experience role template and constituent preview found no corresponding engine or lifecycle API. Package blast-radius preview is a different operation.

features.title: Authorization catalog upgrade review
features.description: Keep granted access tied to installed authorization catalog versions and require review when an upgrade widens or breaks access.
user_capabilities: Inspect a pending catalog migration
Approve the exact widening change
Retain compatible grants across a non-widening upgrade
features.core_note: Registration snapshots installed provenance and revision. Compatible changes restamp grants with audit; widening or breaking changes are refused until the exact migration is reviewed and applied.
features.rust_note: Bounded crates source search for authorization catalog migration/revision review found no counterpart. Rust package preview/activation and version fingerprints do not establish migration of human role grants.

List and revoke owned tokens
Inspect the token-authenticated principal
features.core_note: Tokens are shown once and stored as hashes with owner RLS, expiry and verified issuer. Legacy rows keep an absent issuer rather than inventing one. Bound node and location tokens take separate restricted rails.

user_capabilities: Start or end guest mode
Explore allowed demonstration applications
Use seeded guest data under a guest identity
features.core_note: Guest routes, cookie identity, capability matrix and guard apply a separate guest namespace, deny restricted tiers and seed guest-owned records. The deployment must enable this surface; ordinary anonymous requests do not inherit a real person.
features.rust_note: Daemon seeds a configured guest principal and package tier matrix. Core guest start/end cookie ceremony, package-owned demonstration seed graph and capability matrix are not reproduced by that narrower anonymous admission mechanism.

features.title: Activated application service principals

Activate a service with reviewed grants
Revoke a service activation
features.core_note: Activation service records the principal and narrow permission grants; declarations alone do not run jobs. Current activation and authorization are resolved on each tick, with no inherited swarm administration or management scopes.
features.rust_note: Rust Activations binds declared schedules to user/system principals and records suspension reasons. It is a real engine analogue; reviewed core app-service activation endpoints and exact catalog-permission grant lifecycle were not located in the inspected Rust router.

features.title: Personal data vault encryption and exact-owner storage
features.description: Store a person’s private graph and data in a validated owner-specific vault layout with sensitive-field encryption.

Read supported personal entities and relations
Keep encrypted fields separate from shared data
features.core_note: Vault layout maps exact subjects to bound digest directories and rejects linked leaves; vault field crypto binds encryption to the owner. This is distinct from the administrative HashiCorp Vault console.
features.rust_note: SealedVault implements AES-GCM envelope encryption with per-owner DEKs and references; Rust person-model stores and scoped data cover related personal data. This is not a parity proof for core SQLite graph/vault layout or API.

Read/write/list KV secrets
Issue and revoke scoped leased credentials
Manage policies and database secret roles

features.rust_note: Rust has a sealed secret vault and confirmed master-key rotation endpoint. Inspected vault API does not provide HashiCorp KV/policy/dynamic database lease brokerage or the core console.

Select an explicitly shared tenant connection when allowed
Use own AI credentials with configured fallback policy
features.core_note: Qualified connector brokerage and encryption bind full principal/tenant; callback state is authenticated and one-time. Capability/provider resolution obtains credentials through scoped owner ports, separate from model prompts and application grants.
features.rust_note: Rust personal/shared connection ownership, SecretRef keyring selection and BYO/tenant/operator payer resolution are implemented. Those mechanisms differ from core issuer-qualified connector API and provider-account adoption contracts; live credential isolation was not exercised.

features.title: Interactive tool approvals and protected control events
features.description: Pause tools that require human permission and deliver approval controls without releasing pending protected output.
user_capabilities: Receive task-bound approval request events
Keep ask-mode tools blocked until a decision
Let unanswered requests time out to denial

Source-wide search finds resolveApproval only at its declaration: the modal POSTs /api/tools/approval but the inspected tool router has no decision endpoint. Browser approve/deny completion is therefore not established; normal result events remain completion-gated.
features.rust_note: Rust ToolPolicies and Approvals implement ask/deny/allow, bounded waiting and timeout withdrawal. The inspected HTTP router has one-use confirmations for writes but no task-bound interactive tool-approval delivery/answer surface matching core.

features.title: Signed workload delegation and replay containment
features.description: Delegate exact cross-process user-data operations through recorded short-lived request-bound authority.
user_capabilities: Allow an authorized worker to perform one scoped request
Revoke workload authority
Refuse replayed or mismatched request bindings
features.core_note: Core issues Ed25519-signed claims only after durable workload scope checks; verifier binds method/path/body/audience/issuer and consumes nonce authority. Legacy service-identity handling has explicit containment modes rather than trusting arbitrary user headers.
features.rust_note: Rust Delegations implements HMAC request/body/audience/scope/expiry bindings and in-memory one-use nonces. Bounded api/oshald search found no integration of Delegations redemption into HTTP admission or durable workload authority; this is an implemented primitive, not the wired core cross-process protocol.

features.title: Durable protected remote and inline result authority
features.description: Preserve original grants, package provenance and exact owner through execution and reauthorize before history or output release.
user_capabilities: Open an owned empty protected conversation
Receive only completed currently authorized results
Recover a conversation without bypassing changed grants
features.core_note: Remote permit lifecycle and controller-only startInline/completeInline share durable authority, current owner/policy/snapshot checks and original ceilings. Empty admission requires zero actual messages and current ownership; nonempty no-lineage history remains refused. Inline records are controller provenance, not forged signed worker permits. Current registrations mint a random generation at each API boot, and assertSnapshot requires exact generation equality; prior protected answers are therefore fenced after restart. Stable release identity for durable history remains incomplete.
features.rust_note: Rust dispatch envelopes, node generation/lease checks and owner-scoped task stores provide execution accountability. Bounded control/nodes/orchestration/api search did not locate a durable completed application-result authority equivalent carrying original named grants plus catalog/source snapshot into inline history/SSE release.

features.title: Request identity and PostgreSQL row isolation
features.description: Carry verified request identity into database operations and enforce ownership/tenant access beneath routes.
user_capabilities: Read only rows visible to the request scope
Retain identity across multipart and asynchronous work
Use explicit system identity for authorized background jobs
features.core_note: AsyncLocalStorage carries subject, issuer and operator/system distinction; GUC pool stamps per-client context and strict-mode absence denies. Core includes owner/tenant RLS and least-privilege roles; individual legacy schemas still differ in issuer coverage.
features.rust_note: Rust Ctx derives scope keys and governed roles; documents table enables and forces RLS on scope_key and normal roles are NOBYPASSRLS. Scope construction depends on admitted principal and is separate from credential correctness; no live isolation proof performed in this inventory.

features.title: Untrusted model and scoped tool authority
features.description: Treat model output as untrusted instructions and limit tools/files/providers through code-owned actor and capability scope.
user_capabilities: Use allowed tools inside an authorized task
Keep external content from becoming authority
Write only within an authorized subject/workspace boundary
features.core_note: Capability principal, tool-scope and scoped-file helpers carry restricted actor permissions through execution. Model text cannot supply verified actor or enlarge named permission ceilings; legacy unprotected tools remain separate from catalog-protected operations.
features.rust_note: Rust has untrusted/promoted content types, whole-tuple capabilities, scoped context and workspace claims. These are implemented engine boundaries; parity for all core tool/provider dispatch adapters was not established by their existence.

features.title: HTTP hardening and authenticated callback rails

Use authenticated signed connector callbacks
Inspect CSP reports under administrative controls
features.core_note: CSP defaults to report-only, enforcement is opt-in; body parsers and endpoint limiters have explicit bounds. Manifest routes default to guarded modes and callback exemptions require their own authenticated signature/state rail.
features.rust_note: Rust provides signed webhook/replay checks, fenced egress URL/TLS and OIDC state/PKCE. Inspected API router/lib had no core CSP/reporting or rate-limit preset wiring; compatibility auth_switch still mints synthetic sessions without admission. Current kernel shortcut removal is source-only, not deployment verification.

Assess a finding
Create a remediation ticket

features.rust_note: Bounded crates filename/content search for security-center, secret/dependency/vulnerability scanner and findings APIs found no equivalent scanner/finding workflow. Observe ledger/records are related telemetry, not security scan results.

Receive a device-specific credential once
Verify node ownership before registration

Revoke a lost node credential
Use device APIs without granting full account access

Inspect heartbeat and capability status

Choose an authorized node for work

Device policy includes explicit trusted-system paths rather than silently treating absent user identity as ownership.
features.rust_note: Enrollment visible_to scopes node listing to owner; heartbeat verifies device token and generation, renews lease, and native NodeAgent ticks that rail. Protocol and registry shape differ from core remote-client routes.

features.title: Remote task claim, completion and durable results

Let the node claim its next task
